sq.q: Describe how a queue can be implemented using an array.
answer: A queue is a linear data structure that works on the First In First Out (FIFO) principle. This means that the element that is inserted first will be removed first. In a queue, we insert elements at the rear end and remove elements from the front end.
To implement a queue using an array, we use the following:
An array (say int queue[SIZE]) to store the elements.
Two integer variables: front and rear to keep track of the queue's front and rear positions.
The queue is empty when front == -1 and rear == -1.
On first insertion , both front and rear are set to 0.
Before inserting, check if the queue is full using: rear == SIZE - 1.
If not full: If front == -1, it means it’s the first element, so set front = 0. Increment rear and store the new element at queue[rear].
If front == -1, it means it’s the first element, so set front = 0.
Increment rear and store the new element at queue[rear].
Before deleting, check if the queue is empty using: front == -1 || front > rear.
If not empty: Remove the element at queue[front]. Increment front to point to the next element. If front > rear, reset both front and rear to -1 (queue becomes empty again).
Increment front to point to the next element.
If front > rear, reset both front and rear to -1 (queue becomes empty again).

This means that the first element added to the queue is the first one to be removed. Queues have two ends: the rear (where elements are inserted) and the front (where elements are deleted).
